subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 58-year-old man with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia begins treatment with simvastatin, a structural analog of HMG-CoA that binds the active site of HMG-CoA reductase. Enzyme kinetics are studied in vitro with the drug present and absent. The maximal velocity of the enzyme is unchanged by the drug, but a higher concentration of substrate is needed to reach one-half of the maximal velocity.
question: Which of the following double-reciprocal (Lineweaver-Burk) patterns best describes the inhibited reaction?

options.text: Parallel lines, indicating a decreased Vmax and a decreased Km
Lines that intersect on the y-axis, indicating an increased apparent Km with an unchanged Vmax
Lines that intersect on the x-axis, indicating a decreased Vmax with an unchanged Km
A single line with an increased slope and unchanged intercepts
Lines that intersect to the left of the y-axis, indicating an increased Km and a decreased Vmax

explanation_correct: On a Lineweaver-Burk plot the y-intercept equals 1/Vmax and the x-intercept equals -1/Km. A competitive inhibitor such as simvastatin raises the apparent Km but does not change Vmax, so the y-intercept stays the same while the x-intercept moves toward zero, and the lines intersect precisely on the y-axis. The slope of the inhibited line (Km/Vmax) increases accordingly.

explanation_incorrect.A: Parallel lines are the signature of uncompetitive inhibition, in which both Km and Vmax fall proportionally and the apparent Km actually decreases.
explanation_incorrect.C: Intersection on the x-axis indicates pure noncompetitive inhibition, in which Km is unchanged and Vmax decreases; the vignette describes the opposite pattern.
explanation_incorrect.D: A single line with unchanged intercepts would mean no change in either Km or Vmax, which is inconsistent with the experiment.
explanation_incorrect.E: Intersection to the left of the y-axis indicates mixed inhibition, in which both Km and Vmax change; here Vmax is unchanged.

educationalObjective: A competitive inhibitor produces Lineweaver-Burk lines that intersect on the y-axis because Vmax (1/y-intercept) is unchanged while the apparent Km (1/x-intercept) increases.
